Webhook Delivery Platform: where the project stands

Long image

A

Answer

At commit 60561b0 on main, Phases 1 and 2 are done and Phase 3 has started. Every accepted event is delivered at least once, with retries, a DLQ and a circuit breaker. Limits, secret encryption, the read and replay API, the dashboard and the proof runs are still planned.

  1. An event is accepted atomically, relayed with publisher confirms and fanned out into one job per subscribed endpoint.
  2. The worker signs each job, sends it through an SSRF-safe client, logs the attempt and retries a failure up to 8 attempts.
  3. The circuit breaker parks jobs of a dead endpoint without using up their attempts.
  4. 23 of 48 tasks are done; the 25 open ones are listed below.

3

How does one event travel today?

Diagram structure
  • Tenant tenant
  • Public API api
  • Postgres postgres
  • Outbox relay relay
  • RabbitMQ rabbit
  • Dispatcher dispatcher
  • Worker worker
  • Receiver receiver
  • tenant → api · POST /v1/events
  • api → postgres · insert event, one txn
  • postgres → api · event_id
  • api → tenant · 202 {event_id}
  • relay → postgres · batch, SKIP LOCKED
  • relay → rabbit · publish event
  • rabbit → relay · confirm
  • relay → postgres · mark published, commit
  • rabbit → dispatcher · event
  • dispatcher → postgres · active subscribers
  • postgres → dispatcher · endpoint ids
  • dispatcher → rabbit · job per endpoint
  • rabbit → worker · job
  • worker → postgres · endpoint url, secret
  • worker → receiver · signed POST
  • receiver → worker · 2xx or failure
  • worker → rabbit · failure: retry tier or DLQ
  • worker → rabbit · ack job, only now

Each hop confirms its publish before it acks, so a crash can duplicate a delivery but never lose it. Receivers deduplicate on the stable webhook-id.

4

What can happen to one delivery job?

Diagram structure
  • Queued queued
  • In flight in_flight
  • Delivered delivered
  • In a retry tier retrying
  • Parked parked
  • Dead-lettered dead
  • Skipped skipped
  • Rejected rejected
  • queued → in_flight · worker takes it
  • in_flight → delivered · 2xx
  • in_flight → retrying · failed, attempts left
  • retrying → queued · TTL to retry.ready
  • in_flight → parked · circuit open
  • parked → queued · back on its lane
  • in_flight → dead · 8th attempt failed
  • in_flight → skipped · no call made
  • in_flight → rejected · consumer rejects
  • dead → queued · replay (planned)
5

How does the circuit breaker protect a dead endpoint?

Diagram structure
  • Closed closed
  • Open open
  • Half-open half_open
  • closed → open · ≥ 50% failed
  • open → half_open · cooldown over
  • half_open → closed · probe succeeds
  • half_open → open · probe fails

What should a reader know before relying on this?

Known gaps at this commit

The API returns 500 for ingest while Redis is down, because its rate limiter fails closed. Endpoint signing secrets are still stored in plain text until Task 22. No load test or fault-injection run has been recorded yet, so throughput and latency claims are design targets.
